issues.legal_issue: A law that permits deprivation of property for reasons unrelated to a public purpose is invalid under the constitutional requirement of acquisition or requisition for a public purpose.
material_facts: The statute allowed the government to withhold restoration of property whenever it considered restoration not expedient or practicable, including for reasons other than the stated circumstance that a displaced person occupied the property.
The statute permitted substitution of other property or cash when restoration was withheld, thereby allowing the rightful owner to be deprived of the original property.

Rehabilitation of displaced persons was a public purpose, but the statute also allowed withholding restoration for the government's convenience or the convenience of an occupant who was not a displaced person.
issues.conclusion: The statute violated the public-purpose requirement in Article 31(2) and was invalid.
issues.legal_principle: Article 31(2) required acquisition or requisition to be for a public purpose. Although rehabilitation of displaced persons served a public purpose, a power to deny restoration for governmental or private convenience could also serve a purpose other than a public purpose. The court referred to Amar Singh v. Custodian, Evacuee Property, Punjab for the legislative background; its public-purpose holding rested on Article 31(2).

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_property_dep: A party challenges the constitutionality of a law that permits property to be taken or withheld from its owner.
predicates.law_allows_deprivation_for_nonpublic_con: The law permits property to be withheld from its owner for governmental convenience or the convenience of a private occupant, rather than for a public purpose.

issues.definition: When a challenged property-deprivation law allows deprivation for nonpublic convenience, the law is invalid for lack of a public purpose.

issues.legal_issue: A law providing for deprivation of property is invalid when it neither fixes compensation nor specifies principles and a method sufficient to determine or give compensation.
material_facts: The statute allowed the government to transfer other property said to be nearly of the same value, but did not specify when value was to be assessed.
Alternatively, the statute allowed cash to be paid having regard to the property's value, without requiring payment of the full value or specifying how the amount was to be determined.
After substitute property or cash was granted, the rightful owner's title to the original property was extinguished.
issues.conclusion: The statute failed to provide compensation or principles for determining it as required by Article 31(2), and was invalid.
issues.legal_principle: Article 31(2) required a law to provide for compensation by fixing its amount or specifying the principles on which, and the manner in which, it was to be determined or given. A reference to value without identifying the relevant time for valuation, or permitting cash merely having regard to value without requiring an equivalent amount, did not satisfy that requirement.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_property_dep: A party challenges the constitutionality of a law that permits property to be taken or withheld from its owner.
predicates.law_extinguishes_owner_title: The law provides that the owner's title to the original property is extinguished after the government grants a substitute or payment.
predicates.compensation_amount_or_determination_met: The law does not fix compensation or provide sufficiently definite principles and a method for determining or giving it.

issues.definition: When a challenged law extinguishes the owner's title without sufficiently specifying compensation or how it is determined, the law is invalid for failure to provide compensation.

issues.legal_issue: A law providing alternative means of extinguishing an owner's title cannot be preserved only for cases in which its operation may fall within the constitutional exception for vesting property in the State when the law is not severable.
material_facts: The statute applied both where property remained in the compensation pool, so that extinguishing the owner's title would vest it in the government, and where title had been transferred to a displaced person.
The statute's operation was not severable, and the court had found that it violated Article 31(2).
issues.conclusion: The statute was not severable and had to be declared void as a whole, including in circumstances where the extinguishment might otherwise fall within Article 31(2A).
issues.legal_principle: Article 31(2A) was argued to apply where property vested in a displaced person rather than the government. The court observed that extinguishment could vest property in the government where it remained in the compensation pool, and held that the statute was not severable; it therefore had to be declared void as a whole. No earlier case was relied on for this conclusion.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_property_dep: A party challenges the constitutionality of a law that permits property to be taken or withheld from its owner.
predicates.law_covers_distinct_vesting_outcomes: The law applies both where extinguishing the former owner's title would vest property in the government and where property is held by a private transferee.
predicates.law_is_not_severable: The law's valid and invalid applications cannot be separated from one another.

issues.definition: If a challenged law covers distinct vesting outcomes but cannot be divided into separate applications, it is invalid as a whole.

issues.legal_issue: An appellate court will not entertain a contention that was not raised before the court below.
material_facts: On appeal, counsel for the transferees sought to challenge the order restoring the property on the ground that they had not been heard before it was made.
That contention had not been raised in the High Court.
issues.conclusion: The court did not permit the contention to be raised at the appellate stage.
issues.legal_principle: The court declined to consider a contention raised for the first time on appeal when it had not been taken in the High Court.

predicates.appeal_proceeding: The matter is before a court deciding an appeal from a lower court.
predicates.contention_not_raised_before_lower_court: A party advances a contention on appeal that was not raised before the lower court.

issues.definition: In an appeal, a contention not raised before the lower court is not entertained by the appellate court.
